title: Senior's toolkit: files, text and data
summary: The file, search, JSON, CSV and encoding commands with the switches that prevent the classic accidents.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: files, text and data
steps.body: Most automation is reading some files and writing others. These are the commands, and the one or two switches on each that separate a script that works from one that works on Monday morning.

toolkit.what: Walk folders and return file and folder objects.
flags: fast, done by the file system

toolkit.what: grep with objects: Filename, LineNumber, Line, Matches.
flags: the lines that do not match

toolkit.what: Read and write text files, line by line or whole.
flags: the whole file as one string (JSON, templates)
write exactly what you give it
an array even for one item (7)

toolkit.what: CSV rows as objects, objects as CSV.
flags: add rows to an existing file

toolkit.what: Regex operators built into the language.
Shows a file's raw bytes: the quickest way to see BOMs, UTF-16 and stray characters.
Bulk rename with a script block per file.

steps.prompt: Match the symptom to its fix.
pairs: the file is UTF-16: rewrite it as UTF-8

steps.prompt: Mask passwords in a config before attaching it to a ticket.
steps.explain: `-Raw` reads the file as one string, so the regex also works across line breaks if needed. `-replace` with a literal replacement in single quotes masks every match.

steps.prompt: Which line reads a 2 GB log and keeps only the ERROR lines without loading the whole file into memory?
steps.explain: Piping `Get-Content` streams one line at a time. Parentheses, `-Raw` and assigning to a variable all read the whole file first. (`Select-String -Path .\huge.log -Pattern ERROR` also streams, and is faster still.)

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Say the encoding whenever you write a file other people or systems read. Pass `-Depth` to every `ConvertTo-Json`. Put `-WhatIf` on the first run of anything that renames, moves or deletes in bulk. Use single quotes unless you want something expanded.
